title: Sicilian Defense: Dragon Variation
line: The bishop goes to the long diagonal and aims at the side where White's king often castles.

steps.text: The usual Sicilian start: White pushes the king's pawn, Black answers from the side, and White pushes a second center pawn.
Black trades its side pawn for that center pawn, and both sides bring a knight out.
Push the pawn on g7 one square, to make room for your bishop.

also.a7a6: That is the Najdorf, another main line. This lesson goes on with the Dragon.
also.b8c6: That is the Classical Variation, another main line. This lesson goes on with the Dragon.

steps.text: Put the bishop on g7. Once your knight on f6 moves, it looks along the long diagonal toward White's queen's side.

also.b8c6: That works too. This lesson puts the bishop out first.

steps.text: Castle. The bishop on g7 now guards your king as well.
Bring the other knight out. It hits the knight on d4.
steps.after: White castles on the queen's side and will push pawns at your king.

steps.text: Strike in the center: push the pawn on d6 one square. When your knight takes back, the long diagonal opens for your bishop.
Take back with the knight. Now the bishop on g7 looks down the long diagonal.
Take back with the pawn on b7, toward the center.
steps.after: The pawn left the b-file, so your rooks can use that file against the side where White's king castled.

summary: The Dragon bishop works along the long diagonal, a center pawn push opens it, and a file opens toward White's king.
